title: Grateful Dead Live at Eureka Municipal Auditorium on 1968-01-20

ai_review.summary: Crystal‑clear soundboard capture of a rare pre‑1970 set – first Clementine, Spanish Jam and New Potato – making it a must‑listen for Deadheads.
ai_review.review: The recording is praised as excellent, with every instrument audible and smooth transitions that showcase the band’s improvisational depth. Highlights include the debut performance of “Clementine,” a rare Spanish Jam into Caution, and a spacious rendition of “New Potato” backed by stellar Pigpen keyboards and Jerry’s guitar tone.

ai_rating.rationale: Four out of five reviews give 5‑star praise for both the musical performance (rare songs, tight flow) and the audio quality; only one low rating notes missing track info, not affecting the music or sound.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Reviewers describe the audio as crystal‑clear, with every instrument heard distinctly and no reported mix issues.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Exceptionally smooth transitions; the set weaves jazzy and psychedelic sections together, delivering a cohesive, rare listening experience.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Delivers a spacious New Potato sound; sings on Clementine.
band_member_comments.Phil: Wrote Clementine; noted for his Coltrane‑inspired influence.
band_member_comments.Keys: Pigpen on keyboards is at his best, providing rich textures throughout.
